# Feature: Gender-aware voice design prompt compiler

<!-- auto-generated by /implement on 2026-07-13 -->

## Intent

Voice design must honor female/high/fairy German descriptions instead of producing three identical male voices. Compile Basic DE text into explicit English identity briefs and vary A/B/C within that identity (never contradict gender/pitch).

## Preconditions

- Desktop app with Voicebox sidecar running
- Character voice modal open, Basic tab
- User cleared Advanced fields (or only Basic filled)

## Happy Path

- [ ] Basic `lispelnde frauenstimme hoch und feenhaft` compiles to English with female, high pitch, lisping, fairy-like qualities
- [ ] Candidate B prompt does not request deeper chest / male gravitas when base is female/high
- [ ] A/B/C `design_prompt` values differ but all preserve female-presenting high pitch
- [ ] English Basic descriptions still compile without German prefix wrapper
- [ ] Advanced spec path unchanged (structured compile)

## Edge Cases

- [ ] Male + low German description still gets appropriate male/low variation on B
- [ ] Neutral/ambiguous description uses gender-neutral A/B/C variation (no forced male bias)
- [ ] Prompts stay within Voicebox 2000 char limit

## Regression

- [ ] Zurücksetzen + regenerate candidate still works
- [ ] `compileVoiceDesignPrompt` prefers Advanced spec over Basic when spec non-empty
- [ ] Existing golden spec tests pass

## Assumptions

- Voicebox/Qwen will follow explicit English identity anchors better than raw German + wrapper
- `language: "de"` on profile kept (German speech content); identity brief is English

- `extract-voice-attributes-from-description.ts`: explicit `frauen` / `frauenstimme`
- Layer-1 check (2026-07-13): `lispelnde Frauen feenstimme` → 318-char English brief; Voicebox accepts 3 distinct `design_prompt` values with `Female-presenting`
- If audio still male after this: **Layer 2 (Qwen/Voicebox)** — not Scriptony
